requirement_text: The execution stack runtime order is: chat intake -> context assembly -> intent and plan builder -> proposal compiler -> preview builder -> approval gate -> module adapters -> audit logger.
evidence_ref: No chat intake->context assembly->plan builder->proposal compiler->preview->approval->ADAPTER->audit chain exists. Approval gate and audit logger are real (goldenCaseHappyPath); module adapters and preview builder have no code.

requirement_text: Execution layer owns: adapter dispatch, approval validation, result collection, partial failure handling.
evidence_ref: PROVEN: approval validation (self-approval refused 403; stale decision 409) and result collection (node result acceptance). MISSING: adapter dispatch and partial-failure handling - no adapter layer exists.

requirement_text: Audit layer owns: status trail, actor trail, timestamps, affected artifact refs, final run summary (every run event must be attributable and timestamped).
evidence_ref: PROVEN: every one of 19 chain events is attributable (actor_user_id non-empty, scheduler events stamped system:*) and timestamped, with affected aggregate refs. MISSING: 'final run summary' - there is no Run aggregate to summarise.

requirement_text: Execution Agent must distinguish between planning failure, validation failure, approval missing, adapter execution failure, partial success, and policy/permission failure; user should never receive one flat 'something went wrong' when the system knows which layer failed.
evidence_ref: PROVEN: validation (400 VALIDATION_ERROR), policy/permission (403), wrong-state (409), cross-reference (422) are distinct stable codes - never one flat error. MISSING: adapter execution failure and partial success have no adapter layer to report from.

requirement_text: Reusable runtime pattern from actionDecisionService + actionExecutionAdapter: snapshot before execution, correlation IDs, idempotency checks, explicit execution logs, dry-run style thinking — should be carried into the canonical Run/NodeRun execution model.
evidence_ref: PROVEN: correlation ids end-to-end and idempotency checks (history dedupeKey, wait correlationKey, capability idempotency key). MISSING: pre-execution snapshot and dry-run thinking are not carried into a canonical Run/NodeRun model (no NodeRun table).

requirement_text: Platform must add explicit idempotency and replay-safe execution steps, plus checkpoint and resume packs for long-running work, so retries do not duplicate effects.
evidence_ref: PROVEN: replay-safe commands - a replayed request writes exactly one row (row counts asserted, not response bodies). MISSING: checkpoint/resume packs for long-running work do not exist.

requirement_text: Users and operators must be able to distinguish queued, running, waiting, failed, cancelled and completed work as first-class run/job statuses.
evidence_ref: PROVEN: waiting is first-class and distinguishable from running (wait ACTIVE/EXPIRED, Case BLOCKED). MISSING: queued/running/completed as RUN statuses - there is no canonical Run aggregate.

requirement_text: Invariant 10: Waits, human work and external work are durable first-class runtime semantics.
evidence_ref: A HUMAN wait survives the request that created it (re-read through a fresh app instance and out-of-band from Postgres), is expired later by a separate scheduler actor, and refuses late satisfaction.

requirement_text: Cross-mode invariant: Every mutation has idempotency, readback and audit evidence.
evidence_ref: PROVEN: readback (API response equals out-of-band Postgres row) and audit evidence (outbox) for EVERY mutation in the chain. PARTIAL on idempotency: only commands with a declared primitive (proposals/waits/history/measurements/links/quarantine) are idempotent; status transitions and plan lifecycle rely on expectedVersion OCC alone.

requirement_text: Cross-mode invariant: Approved human work is protected during retry and rerun.
evidence_ref: PROVEN: expiry never manufactures approval - zero decision rows and zero approval.* events after a wait expires; late satisfaction refused 409. MISSING: run-level rerun does not exist, so 'protected during rerun' is untestable.

requirement_text: 'Running' is forbidden for a step that is actually waiting. The step card must identify who/what is awaited, wait start and expected signal, deadline/SLA, last confirmed contact/heartbeat, reminder/escalation policy, next automatic action, impact on the Case, and permitted 'remind', 'reassign', 'skip', 'retry' or 'cancel' actions.
evidence_ref: PROVEN (backend half): a waiting step is never reported as running - wait carries its own status, awaited party (waitType/runId), deadline (dueAt/timeoutAt), and the Case goes BLOCKED. MISSING: the step card itself and remind/reassign/skip/retry actions - no UI.

requirement_text: Live updates: new events never force-scroll a user reading older history; '3 nowe zdarzenia' offers an explicit jump; last confirmed server time remains visible during reconnect; lost connection does not imply a failed Run; duplicate socket/poll events are deduplicated in the UI and runtime.
evidence_ref: Live-update UX (jump-to-new-events, last confirmed server time, reconnect handling). No UI exists.

INBOX side has no implementation, so inbox retry/dead-letter/reconciliation is NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

requirement_text: Wait satisfaction is atomic and unique; duplicate or late events are audited but do not reactivate completed/cancelled Runs.
evidence_ref: PROVEN: satisfaction is unique and final - a late resolve AND a late human-input against an EXPIRED wait are both 409 and leave status=EXPIRED with satisfied_at NULL; nothing reactivates. GAP: the late event is refused but NOT audited - no event is emitted for the refused callback, so 'duplicate or late events are audited' is unmet.

requirement_text: Worker claims use leases/heartbeats; expired leases are reclaimed only after idempotency or reconciliation checks.
evidence_ref: Covered by the sibling service suite (passing on the same real PG): claimTimerWait sets owner token and lease expiry, bumps a monotonic fencing token, and a second concurrent attempt is rejected leaving the row unchanged; resolveWait CAS-fences a lost claim. Not exercised through HTTP because these are scheduler-only and deliberately unrouted.

requirement_text: Cross-mode invariant: Every mutation has idempotency, readback and audit evidence.
implementation_path: server/src/routes/caseWorkspace/**|src/components/CaseWorkspace/api.ts (send + runCommand: mutate -> readback -> render the readback)
evidence_ref: LIVE-U4 RUN 2026-08-10 18:38-18:55 CEST (real Chromium -> Vite :3010 -> backend :3001 [NODE_ENV=development, CI=true, ENABLE_V8_GLOBAL=true; E2E_MODE and ENABLE_TEST_AUTH_BYPASS NOT set] -> Postgres 127.0.0.1:55432/case_workspace_test; session from a REAL POST /api/auth/login; no window.fetch stub, no fixtures, no demo/staging DB). THE INVARIANT IS NOW OBSERVED ON A CROSS-MODE PATH (UI -> API -> DB), not only inside the backend chain. REAL COMMAND FROM THE PRODUCTION UI: row kebab -> "Wstrzymaj zlecenie" -> confirmation -> POST /api/v8/case-workspace/cases/case-0006f4a5-7fa9-41d8-aa0d-793b6cb4b3c0/status -> 200 (Idempotency-Key sent by src/components/CaseWorkspace/api.ts send()), immediately followed by GET /cases/case-0006f4a5-... -> 200 as the readback; out-of-band DB: case_status ACTIVE v6 -> BLOCKED v7; outbox: case.blocked|cw-local-user|2026-08-10T16:46:37.009Z.
